lore.meridian_brewing.wood_elixir:
Come, sit yourself down by the hearth fire and bake off that swamp damp. This old woman has spent a lifetime brewing broths in these soggy marshes, and my old bones have grown as brittle as waterlogged rotted wood. Today I've gathered my wits to tell you the recipe, plain and true, for the wood element among the Five Elements elixirs, known as Green Vine Elixir. Rumor has it an old herb-gatherer from the past dynasty puzzled it out under an ancient vine-choked tree deep in the old woods. Swallow it down, and it turns into a breath of pure vitality from the green growth.

To brew this medicine, you must first read through the parchment with the recipe written on it, and then carefully study the brewing scroll to learn the brewing form. As for these precious things, if you aren't blessed enough to stumble upon a newly built witch hut in the swamp, you'll have to rely on your own skill to best those witches of the True Qi realm and snatch them away. Once you read that parchment, it's etched into your heart, and the paper won't wear out. But mark my words: this Green Vine Elixir has a fierce, stubborn temper. You can't cut corners; you have to watch over the cauldron and brew it with your own two hands.

Now, you can't brew without a cauldron. Beating 7 copper ingots together will fashion you a copper cauldron. It holds 3 portions of water and turns out 2 bottles of medicine, but it rusts easily in the open air, and once it rusts, the heat spreads sluggishly. You'll need to rub Honeycomb over it to ward off rust, and if it does rust up, scrape it clean with an axe. If you take 1 copper cauldron and 3 iron ingots, you can hammer out a witch cauldron; it holds 2 portions of water, yields 1 bottle, and the heat travels much quicker. This medicine calls for pure Yang fire. You can kindle a campfire beneath the cauldron, but a campfire burns right around 100 degrees, can't be adjusted, and its temper is far too fierce. This old woman urges you to set the cauldron on an iron stove. A newly placed iron brazier burns with Yang fire; if it ever turns into Yin fire, grab a handful of sand and pack it in to switch it back. Feed coal or charcoal toward the cauldron as fuel to raise the flame by 1 level and bank 60 seconds of firewood; tap it with a shovel to drop it down 1 level. Raise it up to level 2, and the furnace heat will sit steadily at 85 degrees, swaying by only 1 degree, landing right inside this medicine's heat band of 80 to 88 degrees.

Once your cauldron is propped up, fill it to the brim with clear water first. Other main ingredients usually demand all sorts of painstaking preparation, but this medicine saves you the trouble: gather a fresh Moss Block and pitch the whole block straight into the water. The moment it hits the pot, the recipe is set. Next, toss in 1 portion of base ingredient, Glowstone Dust. Don't you get itchy fingers and go stuffing gunpowder in there; this draught is strictly for swallowing down. If you're hoping to turn it into a splash potion to fling about, the cauldron's mouth simply won't swallow gunpowder. Once it's all in, don't rush to start the brew—let it steep between 40 to 79 degrees for a full 10 seconds, so the vital essence of the herbs can soak out proper.

When it's steeped long enough, take up a stick in your right hand, steady your mind, and perform the brewing form—that marks the start of the brew. A copper cauldron steadily draws 6 yuan of true qi, while a witch cauldron takes 7.8 yuan. It always pulls from the surrounding heaven and earth first; only if that falls short will it sap it from your meridians. If both together aren't enough, you won't even kindle the flame. You brew for a full 30 seconds, and during those 30 seconds, keep your eyes pinned dead onto the cauldron or the hearth fire, and keep your body no more than 3 blocks from the center of the cauldron. Shift your gaze for a split second or take 1 step back, and the fire cuts out on the spot; the ingredients will still sit in the pot, but you'll have to start brewing all over again from scratch.

Keep your hands steady through those 30 seconds. Once the brewing starts, count your way to 8 to 12 seconds, and pinch Glow Berries with your left hand to toss into the cauldron as a secondary ingredient. Then hold your patience until 22 to 26 seconds, and slip the Vines in as the guide herb. Put them in early or late by more than 4 seconds, and most of the medicinal virtue is ruined; leave out the guide herb, and no matter how skilled you are, it will never turn out Superior. Keep a sharp eye on the heat as it brews. An iron stove at level 2 is steady as can be, but if you're using a campfire, any temperature climbing more than 8 degrees above the top of the heat band—that's 96 degrees and up—will scorch it once every 3 seconds. Above 90 degrees, it'll boil away 1 portion of water for nothing every 20 seconds; if the water boils dry, the whole pot scorches black. If the fire gets too fierce, hurry and splash in 1 bottle of cold water to tamp it down; in a copper cauldron, adding 1 bottle drops it by 15 degrees, and in a witch cauldron, it drops by 10 degrees.

When the 30 seconds are up and the herbal steam billows, don't go scrambling like an impatient ape to ladle it out; scooping it while scalding ruins all its spirit. Be patient and wait for the cauldron to cool slowly, falling back between 40 to 79 degrees, before using empty glass bottles to scoop it out bottle by bottle. If the herbs were fresh, the steeping was thorough, the heat stayed locked dead between 80 to 88 degrees, the additions were timed to the split second, it cooled before ladling, and nothing scorched—only then will the bottle bear the mark of Superior. Fall short a bit, and it drops to Fine or Common, with the worst being Poor. And if it can't even scrape together the bones of Poor, all you'll ladle out is a blackened mess of dregs.

Once it's brewed, drinking it does a world of good, sparing you plenty of bitter toil in quiet meditation and breath-work. Down the hatch it goes, and right then and there a share of wood true qi dissolves, surging straight into your opened meridians that belong to wood, such as the Liver meridian and Gallbladder meridian. A Poor brew yields 0.6 yuan, a Common one gives 1 yuan, Fine brings 1.5 yuan, and if it's that entirely emerald Superior draught, you get a full 2.4 yuan. Mind you, if you haven't opened a single meridian belonging to wood, or if your meridians are already brimming with true qi, the draught's power will just scatter uselessly into heaven and earth, leaving not a drop behind.

Yet this spiritual qi of the green wood has a fierce bite, leaving behind an elixir toxin called Sinew Swell. Your sinews swell up stiff and numb; from the instant it reaches your belly, your strikes are slowed by 10% for a full 300 seconds, and not even sweet milk can wash that aching swell away. Before this tier of Sinew Swell clears out, if you get greedy and guzzle another bottle, only half the true qi from the new draught can be gathered into your meridians, and the Sinew Swell immediately deepens to the second tier, forcing you to endure another 300 seconds from the start. By then, your strikes are slowed by a full 20%. If you still don't stay your hand and drink a third bottle, you'll still only glean half the true qi, but the Sinew Swell stacks to the third tier, slowing your strikes by a full 30% until twitching a finger feels as heavy as lead. There are only three tiers to Sinew Swell; drink any more at that point, and you won't gain a speck of true qi, while having to suffer through 300 seconds from the beginning all over again for nothing!

Still, there is one blessing: each of the Five Elements elixirs breeds its own toxin, keeping entirely to itself. Even if you're carrying the poison left by another elixir, it won't stop you from drinking this one. Mark this old woman's words well: before trading blows or dueling spells with someone, if you're in a pinch to use wood arts, downing 1 bottle spares you the slow work of meditation. But while Sinew Swell weighs upon you and your hands are slow, never go locking horns with an enemy up close. Drink 1 bottle, and wait out the full 300 seconds like an honest soul for the elixir toxin to scatter before touching a second bottle. The road of cultivation is long; bite off more than you can chew, and you'll cripple those fine bones and sinews of yours for good.

lore.meridian_brewing.water_elixir:
Come on, sit close to the fire pit, let Granny ramble on and tell you all about it. The dampness by this deep pool is heavy; these old bones ache whenever the rainy days set in, but funny enough, all the good stuff of the water has to be brewed right in chilly, damp places like this. The brew I am teaching you today is called Dawnwell Elixir. It is the water one among our Five Elements elixirs, meant to be kept in clean glass bottles and swallowed down. Mind you now, its bite sinks right into your marrow; it must be drunk down mouthful by mouthful, and do not you ever get the idea of tossing gunpowder into the cauldron to turn it into a splash potion—even if you grab a fistful of gunpowder and try to shove it in, the broth will not take it, and it simply cannot be thrown in. Back in the day, some hasty youngsters who thought breathing and meditating took too long before casting water arts would rely on drinking this in a pinch. Right on the spot, a surge of water true qi would settle into the body, flowing straight into your opened water meridians like the Kidney meridian and Bladder meridian. But you must not be greedy with it, child; there is plenty of bitter suffering waiting later on.

To brew it, you will first need to master two things in hand. One is the parchment recording this recipe; you have to hold it in your hands and read it thoroughly until every word is burned into your memory. You do not need to tear it up or burn it to ash—put it away properly and you can pass it down to the young ones later. The other thing is that brewing scroll; you must read that through too, and only when you have learned the brewing form inside have you truly stepped through the door. This recipe and scroll were either wrestled from witches of the True Qi realm slain in battle by our elders, or picked up as strokes of luck by scouring newly sprouted witch huts across the swamp and rummaging through worn-out chests.

Next comes the furnace. You have to watch the cauldron and brew it by hand yourself. A copper cauldron hammered from 7 copper ingots can sit over a campfire, holding 3 portions of water and scooping out only 2 bottles of medicine. What is more, it feeds on wild flames; even if you switch to a soul campfire for Yin fire, the heat is locked tight at around 100 degrees and cannot be dialed down, which Dawnwell Elixir simply cannot stomach. Granny tells you to use 1 copper cauldron and 3 iron ingots to forge a witch cauldron, and seat it upon an iron brazier. When you first set down the iron brazier, it burns with a cold Yang fire; you have to pinch some Soul Sand or Soul Soil and feed it in to switch it over to an eerie blue Yin fire. Tossing charcoal or coal into the cauldron raises it by 1 tier, with each piece adding 60 seconds of fuel, while giving the cauldron a tap with an iron shovel lowers it by 1 tier. It has four tiers: 75 degrees, 85 degrees, 93 degrees, and 100 degrees. It is steady as can be, fluctuating by at most 1 degree. For brewing this elixir, keep it set at tier 2, which sits right at 85 degrees.

Preparing the ingredients is easy enough. The main ingredient is Packed Ice. Ordinarily when brewing medicine, the main ingredient must first be processed on a workbench; raw materials will not even fit into the cauldron. What is more, processed herbs are at their peak potency within 3 days; past 3 days, they decline day by day, and starting from the 9th day, only 60 percent of their medicinal power remains. Yet this Dawnwell Elixir happens to be an exception. Its main ingredient, Packed Ice, does not need any processing at all; an entire chunk of raw, freezing Packed Ice freshly chiseled out can go straight into the cauldron.

When brewing, the order must never be muddled. First, pour water into the cauldron. Emptying a water bucket into it gives 3 portions of water, while a water bottle adds 1 portion at a time; a witch cauldron must be filled with 2 portions of water. Once the water is in, cast in the Packed Ice; as soon as the main ingredient drops, the brew you are making is decided. Next comes the base ingredient: take a handful of Glowstone Dust and sprinkle it in. Now do not rush to start the brew just yet. First, let the cauldron temperature sit between 40 and 79 degrees, soaking quietly for a full 10 seconds. A craftsman care is all in this unhurried patience: the ingredients must be fresh, the soaking must be thorough, and only with a solid foundation will the medicinal qualities seep through properly.

Once it has soaked long enough, you begin the brew. Hold a stick in your right hand, fix both eyes firmly on the cauldron, and invoke the brewing form. This brewing takes a full 30 seconds. Throughout these 30 seconds, your body must never step beyond 3 blocks from the cauldron center, and your eyes cannot wander for even a heartbeat; you must stare unblinkingly at the cauldron or the Yin fire beneath it. If your gaze drifts, your feet wander off, or the true qi in your body fails to hold, the brew will snap right then and there. Even if the brew breaks, do not panic: the ingredients and that soaking work from earlier are still stewing in the cauldron, not completely ruined, so you can catch your breath and start the brew again. For a batch like this, a copper cauldron evenly consumes 6 yuan of true qi over 30 seconds, while a witch cauldron burns through 7.8 yuan. If there is not enough true qi in the surrounding world, it will forcefully drain true qi from your opened meridians; if both places together fall short, you will not even be able to start the brew.

Once brewing begins, you must count the seconds in your heart. When you reach the brief window between the 6th second and the 10th second, hold the auxiliary ingredient, Dried Kelp, in your left hand and toss it steadily into the cauldron. Then count along until between the 18th second and the 22nd second, and with your left hand, cast in the catalyst, Prismarine Crystals, dead on time. Both auxiliary and catalyst must be added after brewing starts; neither too early nor too late will do. If your timing is off by within 4 seconds, the potency will be passable, but if you miss by too much, throwing them in is no different than wasting them. Most of all, if you miss tossing in that catalyst Prismarine Crystals, no matter how miraculous your heat control is, you will never brew up a top-tier Superior grade—it will reach Fine at the absolute best.

During the brewing, you must keep your eyes locked on the temperature. The heat range for Dawnwell Elixir is exceedingly narrow, right between 82 and 90 degrees. Setting an iron stove to tier 2 puts it at 85 degrees, landing right in that sweet spot, which saves the most trouble. If the heat gets too fierce and runs more than 8 degrees above 90 degrees, the broth will scorch once every 3 seconds; moreover, as soon as the temperature passes 90 degrees, 1 portion of water will evaporate away every 20 seconds, and if the water boils completely dry, the whole batch is ruined. If the fire flares too high, hurry and add a bottle of cold water to tamp it down: adding a bottle drops the temperature by 10 degrees in a witch cauldron, and by 15 degrees in a copper cauldron.

When the full 30 seconds are up, do not you go rushing to ladle it out. The broth will be bubbling hot; you have to watch the cauldron cool down slowly until it drops between 40 and 79 degrees before taking empty glass bottles to scoop it up, one bottle per scoop, yielding exactly 1 bottle from a witch cauldron. If you lose your patience and scoop it out while it is scalding hot, more than half of its potency will be lost. Whether your craft succeeds or fails all hinges on whether the ingredients were fresh enough, whether the soaking was thorough, whether the heat was steady, whether the auxiliary and catalyst were cast on time, and whether you had the patience to let it cool before scooping. If it scorches even once, the spiritual energy of the whole batch is heavily damaged; and if it is botched beyond hope, all you will scoop up is a mess of dregs.

The elixir you scoop out will show its quality upon the bottle. If you were impatient while brewing, what you get is Poor, and drinking it down gives you only 0.6 yuan of water true qi on the spot; a Common one grants 1 yuan; a Fine one grants 1.5 yuan; and if every step was seamless and the catalyst dropped without a hair of error, the Superior elixir that comes out will send 2.4 yuan of water true qi surging in with a single gulp. But mark my words: if you have not opened a single one of your water meridians, or if your meridians are already filled to the brim with water qi, that swallowed true qi will have nowhere to settle and will dissipate right back into the world for nothing.

Lastly, and most importantly, Granny has to give you a stern warning. This Dawnwell Elixir carries an elixir toxin called Bone Chill. The moment the elixir passes your throat, a freezing chill cuts straight through your bones; even chugging down a bucket of milk will not cure this toxin. You must endure a full 300 seconds before the chill disperses on its own. While Bone Chill clings to you, your legs stiffen up and your walking slows by 10 percent. If some foolish novice feels they lack true qi and rushes to drink a second bottle before the Bone Chill has cleared, they are in for sheer misery: the potency of that second bottle gets scattered by the chill, yielding only half the true qi, while the Bone Chill worsens to the second layer, slowing walking by 20 percent, and you have to suffer through those 300 seconds all over from the start! Bone Chill has three layers in all. If your greed pushes you to the third layer, your walking slows by a full 30 percent, and at that point, even if you drink another drop, you will not gain a single speck of true qi—you will just heap on another 300 seconds of freezing agony for nothing. Fortunately, the Five Elements elixirs each have their own nature; if you are carrying the elixir toxin left behind by another elixir, it will not stop you from drinking this one.

So, taking a sip before casting spells or fighting saves you the tedious chore of sitting with eyes closed breathing and meditating, which is handy indeed. But if you are chasing down an enemy or fleeing for your life, having your legs slowed by 10 percent can easily cost you your head. Do not you ever get greedy: drink one bottle steadily, wait until those 300 seconds have passed and the Bone Chill has cleared away completely, and only then take a second bottle. Have you got all that down? If you do, go fetch two blocks of Packed Ice, and Granny will watch you light the fire.

lore.meridian_brewing.earth_elixir:
Come, sit closer to the stove and warm your hands. The damp runs heavy in this swamp and the muddy water clings to your feet, but buried under those murky mire pools are all the treasures of us brewing folk. Today, this old woman is going to pass down an old recipe to you: Earth Marrow Elixir. It is the one that walks the earth path among our Five Elements elixirs, sitting heavy and solid inside a glass bottle. Folks who practice earth cultivation arts cherish it most of all; drinking down a bottle before casting some grand divine ability saves them the bitter toil of meditating in seclusion half the day just to gather earth true qi. Years ago, when this old woman was chased hard by venomous spiders over in that muddy hollow, it was this elixir propping up my earthen true qi that saved this old life of mine.

If you want to brew this elixir, you must first have two things in hand. One is the parchment with this recipe written upon it, which you must take and read through thoroughly from end to end. The other is a brewing scroll, for only after reading it will you understand how to raise the brewing form. As for those two treasures, either you duel a witch of the True Qi realm one day and search them off her body after winning, or you head deep into the swamp to try your luck, seeking out newly raised witch huts to rummage through their chests.

This brew is picky about its heat; it can only be brewed over Yang fire. Since you are just learning the craft, if you only have a copper cauldron on hand, set it over a campfire. A campfire is ready-made Yang fire, but its temper is wild, its heat leaping around 100 degrees year-round with no way to adjust it. Later on, when your craft grows finer, forge a witch cauldron out of a copper cauldron and 3 iron ingots, and set it on an iron stove. An iron brazier burns with Yang fire when freshly placed down; if someone switches it to Yin fire, you just toss a handful of sand onto it to turn it back into Yang fire. That iron brazier is mighty handy: use coal or charcoal targeting the cauldron to shift up, or use a shovel targeting it to shift down. Set it to gear 2, and the heat rests right at 85 degrees, as steady as can be. It recognizes the earthy touch of human hands, so you must watch the cauldron and brew it by hand yourself.

As for gathering ingredients, this brew is the most considerate to us herb-gatherers. Other main ingredients cannot do without chopping, grinding, and sun-drying, for raw materials cannot enter the cauldron at all, yet the main ingredient for Earth Marrow Elixir is nothing other than Clay Balls dug straight from mud pits—no processing needed, just dig them up and drop them right into the cauldron. Aside from that, you must ready Bone Meal as an auxiliary ingredient, pick a fresh Brown Mushroom to serve as a guide herb, and keep a pinch of Glowstone Dust at your side for the base ingredient. Bear in mind, this medicine is meant to be drunk into the belly gulp by gulp and cannot touch a speck of gunpowder. If your hand trembles and you try tossing gunpowder into the cauldron, the cauldron will reject you on its own and refuse to take it in.

When brewing, the order must not be muddled in the slightest. First, pour in the water. Use a water bucket to pour it into the copper cauldron—exactly 3 portions of water at a time, which yields 2 bottles of medicine; if it is a witch cauldron, fill it with 2 portions of water to yield 1 bottle of medicine. Once the water is filled, toss in the Clay Ball first. Once the main ingredient is in, the recipe for this batch is set. Next comes the base ingredient, Glowstone Dust. If the fire's temperature is between 40 and 79 degrees at this moment, do not rush to begin brewing; let the ingredients soak steadily in the warm water for 10 seconds. Only when soaked through will the medicinal potency come out rich and thick.

The moment you start the brew, hold a stick in your right hand, fix your eyes firmly upon the cauldron, and cast the brewing form. A copper cauldron consumes 6 yuan of true qi for a batch, while a witch cauldron consumes 7.8 yuan of true qi, drawn away evenly little by little over these 30 seconds. The cauldron first borrows spiritual energy from the surrounding world, and if there is not enough in the world, it deducts it from the opened meridians in your own body. During these 30 seconds of brewing, you cannot wander more than 3 blocks away from the center of the cauldron, and not for a single instant may your eyes leave the cauldron body or the fire beneath it. If you turn your head to look elsewhere, the batch will not be ruined entirely—the herbs and the soaking work will still remain—but the brewing momentum will break, and you will have to spend true qi to start brewing all over again.

In these 30 seconds, the timing of adding ingredients is more precious than gold. Watch the clock closely: between seconds 6 to 10 after starting the brew, pinch up the Bone Meal with your left hand and toss it in; come seconds 18 to 22, toss that Brown Mushroom in with your left hand. If the guide herb is left out, no matter how skilled you are, you will not brew Superior medicine. Being off by within 4 seconds when adding ingredients is barely passable, but if you are off by too much, the auxiliary ingredient and guide herb will dissolve into the water for nothing.

Your eyes must keep a tight watch on the heat, too. Earth Marrow Elixir only honors that temperature band between 84 and 92 degrees. Gear 2 on an iron brazier sits right at 85 degrees, fitting snugly inside it. If you use a campfire, the heat reaches 100 degrees, more than 8 degrees higher than the top of that temperature band. Every 3 seconds, the brew will scorch once, and each scorching damages its medicinal potency by a hefty margin. What is more, as long as it exceeds 90 degrees, 1 portion of water will boil away into steam for nothing every 20 seconds, and once the water boils dry, the whole cauldron will scorch through and through. When the campfire burns too fiercely, quickly take a water bottle and add a bottle of cold water to the cauldron to suppress it; adding one bottle lowers a copper cauldron by 15 degrees, and a witch cauldron by 10 degrees.

Once you have brewed it for the full 30 seconds and the medicinal aroma drifts out, do not rush to ladle it out just yet. Wait until the cauldron slowly cools down and drops to between 40 and 79 degrees before stepping up with empty glass bottles to scoop it out bottle by bottle. If you are impatient and ladle it while it is scalding hot, the medicinal potency will suffer as well.

Whether your craft is clumsy or fine is written right upon those medicine bottles. With fresh ingredients, soaked for a full 10 seconds, heat kept steady between 84 and 92 degrees, ingredients added without the slightest error, and scooped only after cooling down, what you brew will be lustrous Superior medicine. A bit short of that, you will still get Fine or Common, but if the heat runs wild and the ingredients are added all wrong, you will end up with nothing but Poor medicine, or even scoop out a puddle of dregs.

Drink down this medicine, and right on the spot a mellow surge of earth true qi rushes straight into your earth meridians, like the Spleen meridian and Stomach meridian. If it is Poor, you will only gain 0.6 yuan; Common grants 1 yuan; Fine grants 1.5 yuan; and if you brewed Superior, you will receive 2.4 yuan right then and there. Mind you, if you have not opened a single earth meridian in your body, or if your meridians are already brimming full, drinking this gulp down will just disperse into the world for nothing, without keeping a speck of it.

Lastly, this old woman must give you a stern and solemn warning: effective as this Earth Marrow Elixir is, its elixir toxin is exceedingly heavy. Drinking down a bottle binds your body with a layer of elixir toxin called Leaden Weight, which grinds against you for 300 seconds before slowly dissipating; not even drinking milk can purge it. While Leaden Weight is upon you, your whole body feels mired in mud, and your jumps are two-tenths lower. If those 300 seconds have not passed and you greedily gulp down another bottle for the sake of true qi, the true qi from that bottle will be cut in half on the spot, Leaden Weight will worsen to the second layer, making your jumps four-tenths lower, and the 300 seconds of elixir toxin will reset from the beginning. Should you recklessly drink a third bottle, Leaden Weight will deepen to the third layer: not only will you jump low, you will not even be able to break into a run, left only to shuffle step by step. At that point, even if you drink the elixir like water, you will not wring out a single scrap of true qi—you will purely be heaping on 300 seconds of suffering for nothing.

But do not you fret too much. The elixir toxins of these Five Elements each walk their own path without meddling with one another; carrying the toxin left by another elixir will not get in the way of drinking this one. Just remember: after finishing a bottle, wait honestly for 300 seconds until the crust of mud upon you clears away completely before drinking the next, and never be greedy. Off you go now—take your stick and Clay Balls, and try your hand at a batch before the furnace.

codex.intro.meridian_brewing.brewing: An old brewing craft kept in stilt huts deep within the marsh. Following rim grooves and shifting ash, it simmers a pot full of potent draughts.
codex.power.meridian_brewing.brewing_bas: Know the warmth held within the black, white, and red ash beneath the stove. Run a wooden spoon along the pot's rim groove, balancing the heat in three steady turns.
